Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates bilateral lateral displacement of the paraspinal lines (indicated by arrowheads) forming a smooth, widened lower posterior mediastinal mass without vertebral destruction or respiratory symptoms. This radiographic appearance is characteristic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (or other lymphoproliferative disorders) presenting as a paravertebral mass, distinguishing it from neurogenic tumors which are typically unilateral and may cause bone erosion.
